title: Legacy response to pump seal leakage
content: Superseded revision. For a running centrifugal pump with a visible seal leak, continue operation until leakage exceeds 20 drops per minute. Inspect vibration at the next scheduled round. This revision was replaced by PROC-PUMP-017-R3.

title: Current response to pump vibration and seal leakage
content: Current approved revision. When a running centrifugal pump has increasing vibration together with visible seal leakage, notify the control room and maintenance planner, establish an exclusion boundary, and perform a condition assessment before continued operation. Do not rely on a drops-per-minute threshold. A qualified person must decide whether shutdown is required. Record observations; do not infer a root cause from these symptoms alone.

title: Centrifugal pump condition assessment evidence
content: Collect vibration velocity by axis, bearing temperature, seal leakage observations, suction and discharge pressure, and recent trend history. Compare measurements with the asset-specific approved limits. This guide does not define a universal shutdown threshold and does not provide fastener torque values.

title: Maintenance stock reservation policy
content: A planner may review stock availability but must not treat quantity on hand as reserved stock. Parts are reserved only after an approved work order and storeroom confirmation. Low-stock items require a replenishment check before scheduling. The assistant is not authorized to reserve or issue parts.

title: Compressor oil separator replacement
content: For a rotary screw compressor, isolate and verify zero energy before replacing the oil separator. Confirm the replacement element against the equipment bill of material. A qualified maintainer must complete the replacement and post-maintenance leak check.
